teams.name: Eona

in.name: Petr Velenko
in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: The national champions went 14-3, beating Ranroman State 30-14 in the Great Fourteen final and Dietsche 56-24 at Palm Creek after a 31-28 semifinal win over Tasson. Four first-round picks left, defensive lineman Nanami Sasagawa at No. 8, linebacker Emeka Belloni, running back Kyriaki Chrypoulos and lineman Demetrius Akisei, among 11 draftees in all. Hollis Upshaw's fifth year brings in five-star lineman Tyrell Kingsmond and quarterback Petr Velenko from Costique State, and Dietsche comes to Eona in week 3 in a rematch of the title game.

teams.note: An 11-4 year ended in the quarterfinals, 34-17 to Pistolheart at the Lumber Bowl, after a 30-14 loss to Eona in the Great Fourteen final and a 55-7 second-round win over Marblehead. Defensive lineman Omar Geortellis went fifth overall. Litowa Mesteniy's fourth year starts at home against Skeenerland State in week 0, adds five-star quarterback Dulce Navamayor and transfer quarterback Adelheid Solland from Kaji Kita State, and ends with Pistolheart at home in week 13 and a trip to Ranroman in week 14.

teams.note: A 15-2 season took Dietsche to the national title game: a 42-23 win over Tasson in the Jyras Bay final, then wins over Trapper Point, Hoganelle and Pistolheart before the 56-24 loss to Eona. Sora Yamamoto's fifth year keeps the same coordinators, Itsuki Tachibana and Baltazar Albamayor, each also in a fifth year. Five-star linebacker Uchenna Zamorano is the headline freshman and punter Magnus Apotzis arrives from Coachville. The schedule includes a week-3 trip to Eona and Antiragal State in week 7.

teams.name: Rogaela State

out.name: Margaux Malfour
out.reason: didn't fit the new staff's plans

teams.note: An 8-4 year, 5-4 in Jyras Bay play, missed the postseason. Rami Campbell is in his 16th year, but the offense changes hands: Carlos Lopez left to coordinate the defense at Central Stanton, and Brunhilde Stanhope arrives from Kaji Daun as offensive coordinator. Five-star linebacker Howahkan Laufanua leads a class of 18. Dietsche is the week-14 finale.

teams.name: Barhold
teams.note: An 11-4 year ended in the quarterfinals, 38-17 to Tasson at the Redwood Bowl, after wins over Vaughn Bay State (41-10) and UFNH (48-23). Cornerback Adjoa Ezesah went 28th overall. Darnell Ellery's fourth year has a new defensive coordinator in Ettore Albareal and five-star lineman Ghislaine Vignascio in the class. Skeenerland State visits in week 6 and Barhold goes to Marblehead in week 7.

in.reason: didn't fit the new staff's plans

teams.note: An 11-3 year, 8-1 in Western Coast play, ended with a 33-31 loss to Yrei Trobniy in the conference final and a 34-23 second-round loss to Hoganelle. Svetlana Wright's fifth year has a new defensive coordinator in Poppy Hollerbach, and five-star lineman Dieter Eisenhuber heads a class of 17. The season opens at home against Orlot in week 0 and closes with Burrstone; Yrei Trobniy is a week-13 trip.

teams.name: Crayellan
teams.note: A 9-6 year was a playoff run: Crayellan beat Fiota Bay 27-20 in the Mountain Valley final, beat Hatesei 17-14 in round one, and lost to Eona 36-27 in the second round. Ximena Carrasco's sixth year has Axel Osterberg in as defensive coordinator, and safety Sunita Gangaraj went 36th overall as an early entrant. A week-3 trip to Tasson and a week-9 trip to Fiota Bay are the marquee road games.

teams.name: Pistolheart
teams.note: An 11-4 year, 6-3 in the Great Fourteen, reached the semifinals: wins over Yrei Trobniy (35-20) and Ranroman State (34-17), then a 28-13 loss to Dietsche at the Steam Bowl. Pistolheart is still looking for its first national title. Ten players were drafted, including lineman Honoka Harukami at No. 25. Tage Ludendorf's third year brings five-star tight end Mireille Ashwell, and the schedule is among the hardest on this list, with Ranroman State away in week 13 and Central Stanton at home in week 14.

teams.name: North Hatesei

in.name: Sidney Theokidis
in.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: The most decorated program in the country, with 21 titles and the latest in 2030, went 7-5 and missed the postseason. Perla Notaro arrives as head coach after being poached from Eternal Fox, where she went 8-5. Wide receiver Ikaika Highknife comes in from Costique State, and the class is small, 11. Eona visits in week 6 and the season closes at home against Hatesei.

teams.name: Ranroman
teams.note: An 8-5 year ended in round one, 30-24 at home to Yrei Trobniy. Offensive coordinator Vika Lameotter left to become head coach at Orlot and Adelheid Ostrenko takes over the offense for Ghislaine Penahermosa's third year. Running back Zlata Radushkin transfers in from Kaji Daun. The year opens at Will Tech in week 0, goes to Eona in week 11 and ends at home against Ranroman State.

teams.note: A 7-5 year, 6-3 in the Great Fourteen, missed the postseason. Boris Walker is in his ninth year and Carlos Lopez arrives from Rogaela State as defensive coordinator. The recruiting class is only five players, led by five-star linebacker Kanei Lorresei. The finish is demanding: Eona in week 13 and a trip to Pistolheart in week 14.

Quarterback Peizhi Liangyan comes in from Costique. The schedule opens with Diamond City in week 2 and goes to Barhold in week 4 and Skeenerland State in week 11.

Ekralund State visits in week 6, Eastern State goes to Ciarralotta Tech in week 7 and finishes at Keeper.

teams.name: Skylar Rose
teams.note: The 2041 champions went 8-4 and missed the postseason. Amir Chen is in his seventh year; defensive lineman Maximo Penalarga went 54th and lineman Svyatoslav Jasnanov 60th. Hatesei is the week-1 visitor, Park Island is a week-10 trip, and Southern Tengus is the finale at home.

teams.name: Hatesei
teams.note: A 9-4 year ended in round one, 17-14 at home to Crayellan. Freya Dahlqvist's second year faces the second-hardest schedule of the 152 programs, opening at Skylar Rose in week 1, going to Eona in week 4 and ending at North Hatesei. Safety Auvenniy Mesreniy went 31st overall and quarterback Elharith Geortzis comes in from Chinolka.
